```plato
//==
// # Kinematics
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Kinematics
//  - Trajectories and elementary motions

//==
// # Kinematics
//
// Motion state described without reference to forces or mass: instantaneous
// linear and angular states, spatial velocities (twists), and spatial forces
// (wrenches). Unless a doc comment says otherwise, linear quantities are in
// meters and seconds and angular quantities are in radians and seconds.

//==
// # Instantaneous motion state

// The instantaneous linear motion of a point in the plane. Position is in
// meters; Velocity is in meters per second; Acceleration is in meters per
// second squared.
type KinematicState2D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Position: Point2D;
    Velocity: Vector2D;
    Acceleration: Vector2D;
}

// The instantaneous linear motion of a point in space. Position is in meters;
// Velocity is in meters per second; Acceleration is in meters per second
// squared.
type KinematicState3D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Velocity: Vector3D;
    Acceleration: Vector3D;
}

// The instantaneous rotational motion of a planar body: orientation angle,
// signed angular velocity, and signed angular acceleration (counterclockwise
// positive).
type AngularState2D
    implements IValue
{
    Orientation: Angle;
    AngularVelocity: AngularVelocity;
    AngularAcceleration: AngularAcceleration;
}

// The instantaneous rotational motion of a spatial body. AngularVelocity is
// in radians per second about each world axis (axis-scaled rotation rate);
// AngularAcceleration is in radians per second squared about each world axis.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_velocity)
type AngularState3D
    implements IValue
{
    Orientation: Quaternion;
    AngularVelocity: Vector3D;
    AngularAcceleration: Vector3D;
}

// The full kinematic state of a planar rigid body: pose plus linear and
// angular rates. LinearVelocity is in meters per second; LinearAcceleration
// is in meters per second squared; angular rates are counterclockwise
// positive.
type RigidKinematicState2D
    implements IValue
{
    Pose: Pose2D;
    LinearVelocity: Vector2D;
    AngularVelocity: AngularVelocity;
    LinearAcceleration: Vector2D;
    AngularAcceleration: AngularAcceleration;
}

// The full kinematic state of a spatial rigid body: pose plus linear and
// angular rates. LinearVelocity is in meters per second; LinearAcceleration
// is in meters per second squared; AngularVelocity is in radians per second
// and AngularAcceleration in radians per second squared, each about the
// world axes.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigid_body)
type RigidKinematicState3D
    implements IValue
{
    Pose: Pose3D;
    LinearVelocity: Vector3D;
    AngularVelocity: Vector3D;
    LinearAcceleration: Vector3D;
    AngularAcceleration: Vector3D;
}

//==
// # Spatial velocity and force

// A planar spatial velocity: the linear velocity of a reference point in
// meters per second, plus the body's signed angular velocity
// (counterclockwise positive). Known as a twist in screw theory.
type SpatialVelocity2D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Linear: Vector2D;
    Angular: AngularVelocity;
}

// A spatial velocity: the linear velocity of a reference point in meters per
// second, plus the angular velocity in radians per second about each axis.
// Known as a twist in screw theory.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screw_theory)
type SpatialVelocity3D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Linear: Vector3D;
    Angular: Vector3D;
}

// A planar spatial force: a force in newtons acting at a reference point,
// plus the signed out-of-plane torque (counterclockwise positive).
// Known as a wrench in screw theory.
type SpatialForce2D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Force: Vector2D;
    Torque: Torque;
}

// A spatial force: a force in newtons acting at a reference point, plus a
// torque in newton-meters about each axis. Known as a wrench in screw theory.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torque)
type SpatialForce3D
    implements IValue, IInterpolatable
{
    Force: Vector3D;
    Torque: Vector3D;
}

//==
// # Trajectories and elementary motions
//
// Motion described over time: time-sampled trajectories, and the closed-form
// elementary motions (ballistic flight, uniform circular motion, harmonic
// oscillation, and the pendulum). Unless a doc comment says otherwise, linear
// quantities are in meters and seconds and angular quantities are in radians
// and seconds.

//==
// # Sampled trajectories

// A time-sampled planar motion stored as parallel arrays: Times[i] is the
// time since trajectory start, Positions[i] the position in meters, and
// Velocities[i] the velocity in meters per second. Velocities may be empty
// when unknown.
type Trajectory2D
    implements IValue
{
    Times: Array<Duration>;
    Positions: Array<Point2D>;
    Velocities: Array<Vector2D>;
}
```
